budget_items.what_was_said: Equipment for the school HVAC system is on site and installation will begin once school ends; the school committee already voted to fund the district's portion, though the state/grant funding doesn't kick in until July 1.

Two refrigeration projects and a controls project were approved with no town dollar contribution, funded entirely through Unitil incentives and the Green Grant; the chair wants the facilities director to move faster since it costs the town nothing.

budget_items.topic: Town Hall and Ritter HVAC upgrades (capital plan)
budget_items.what_was_said: HVAC upgrades at Town Hall and Ritter were approved on the capital plan funded starting July 1; the facilities director favors buying individual mini-split units for staff to install rather than a full building control system to avoid prevailing wage costs.

budget_items.topic: MRPC annual report and grant-writing services
budget_items.what_was_said: Karen and her MRPC team were retained for another stretch covering two years of annual reports and one more grant-writing round.
A Facebook post reported the savings from the street light conversion project using before-and-after cost data provided by the chair.

budget_items.topic: Street light project ROI / purchase cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The town is nearing the payback point on buying the streetlight infrastructure itself (the rest was grant-funded); the purchase price rose during negotiations.
A smaller town converting 30 street lights did not purchase the infrastructure and must keep paying Eversource for maintenance, which was described as roughly half the old cost burden.
The facilities director gave a rough cost for a new building control system for the library, for controls alone; the library does not want mini-splits for aesthetic reasons.
The chair cited an example cost quoted to fix a malfunctioning control device as too high, to argue the facilities director needs better in-house understanding of building control systems.
A prior capital plan figure for cruiser funding was discussed, with a matching purchase expected in 2026 under a plan just approved at town meeting; word is the cruisers came in under budget.
The chair criticized municipal procurement rules, using a hypothetical appropriation to illustrate how vendors tailor bids to whatever budget is announced rather than bidding first.

decisions.decision: April 7th meeting minutes tabled to the next meeting because Chris had not yet reviewed them.
Chair will push the facilities director to get the no-cost refrigeration and controls projects (Unitil/Green Grant funded) completed soon.
Chair will follow up with Caesar about changing committee member status wording from 'associate' to 'alternate'.
Chair plans to bring Tyler before the select board, likely the following Tuesday, for associate/alternate member appointment.
Members told that reappointment is not automatic and Matt must contact the selectman's office to confirm he is re-upping.
Next meeting set for July 7th, planned as an in-person meeting with Zoom available.

minutes.headline: Committee pressed the schools and town to actually use already-approved, no-cost green energy grant funding.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force reviewed the status of school and town energy projects funded through incentives, grants, and the capital plan, with no town money required for several of them, and pushed the school facilities director and other town departments to move faster. The committee also discussed member appointment and term-length irregularities, recruited prospective new members, and adjourned by roll-call vote after setting its next meeting for July.

what_happened.line: The chair pushed the school facilities director to finish two refrigeration projects and a controls upgrade that cost the town nothing, funded by Unitil incentives and the Green Grant.
Members flagged irregularities in how associate and alternate committee members are appointed and termed, and will raise wording changes with the town.
School HVAC equipment is on site and installation begins once school ends, though the state and grant funding for it does not start until July 1.
The committee tabled approval of its April 7th minutes because a member had not yet reviewed them.
The next meeting was set for July 7th, in person with a Zoom option, closing by roll-call vote.

why_it_matters: Several energy-efficiency projects at schools and town buildings are already approved and grant-funded at no cost to taxpayers, so delay in completing them is a lost-savings issue, not a budget one.
How the town appoints and terms task-force members (associate versus alternate status, five- versus seven-member structure) affects who can serve and vote on this committee going forward.
Capital-plan HVAC work at Town Hall and Ritter, and a possible library building-control system, will show up as future capital budget items residents may be asked to fund.
